scope: 73 cleaned TRACE PIAs; exploratory content characterization only
discovery_topic_names: Data minimization and retention lifecycle management
Identity authentication and least-privilege access control
Encryption and physical or secure-transfer safeguards
refinement_decision: Retained eight control-mechanism themes and explicit boundary rules, especially minimization-versus-retention, access-versus-use controls, and operational-security-versus-organizational-assurance distinctions.

topics.name: Data minimization and identifiability reduction
topics.definition: A control reduces the amount, sensitivity, identifiability, visibility, or concentration of information collected, derived, processed, displayed, tested, or released.
inclusion_rule: constrained fields, free text, or populations
exclusion_rule: access restrictions that preserve the same data
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Less data or less identifiable data means M01; fewer people reaching unchanged data means M02; lifecycle-ended deletion means M05.

topics.name: Identity, authentication, and least-privilege access
topics.definition: A control verifies identity or authority and limits access, privileges, records, or functions to approved people with a legitimate role or need.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Who may access what means M02; what an authorized user or recipient may do means M03; observing what a user did means M04.

topics.name: Purpose, use, sharing, and recipient controls
topics.definition: Legal, policy, contractual, or procedural rules constrain permissible purposes, recipients, disclosures, onward use, and external-party handling.
exclusion_rule: encrypted transfer without a handling rule
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Who may enter means M02; why, how, or to whom data may be used or sent means M03; transformation of released data means M01.

topics.name: Operational security, physical protection, monitoring, and incident handling
topics.definition: Concrete technical, architectural, physical, detective, or response mechanisms protect data and systems in operation and detect, contain, or recover from security events.
exclusion_rule: formal policy, training, and control assessment
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Runtime protection, detection, or response means M04; organizational policy, workforce preparation, or formal assurance means M08.

topics.name: Bounded retention and verified disposition
topics.definition: A control establishes, implements, or verifies time- or event-bounded retention, transfer to archives, return, deletion, overwriting, or destruction.
inclusion_rule: automatic expiry, overwrite, or cache clearing
return or destruction of external copies
exclusion_rule: removal because data was unnecessary at intake
backup and recovery without lifecycle rules
duration without a limiting or disposition action
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Unnecessary content removal means M01; elapsed-time, end-of-purpose, or schedule removal means M05.

topics.name: Transparency, contextual notice, and meaningful choice
topics.definition: A control informs individuals or the public about collection, use, sharing, and available choices, or enables consent, refusal, opt-out, withdrawal, or valid authorization at the relevant decision point.
inclusion_rule: PIA and SORN publication used as notice
exclusion_rule: legal citations or internal policies not communicated to people
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Information and choice before or at collection or use means M06; post-collection inspection, correction, challenge, or remedy means M07.

topics.name: Data quality, individual access, correction, and redress
topics.definition: A control prevents or detects substantive record errors or enables a person to inspect, correct, amend, challenge, appeal, or obtain remedy for maintained information or its consequences.
inclusion_rule: Privacy Act and FOIA access and amendment
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Access to one's own record and correction means M07; employee access to perform work means M02; pre-use choice means M06.

topics.name: Governance, workforce accountability, and formal assurance
topics.definition: Organizational measures establish responsibility, competent handling, enforceable conduct, documented policy, risk and control assurance, and consequences for noncompliance.
inclusion_rule: FISMA, NIST, and RMF assessment or authorization
exclusion_rule: direct runtime security and incident mechanisms
bare legal citations or bare adequacy claims
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Organizational duty, preparation, oversight, or assurance means M08; direct system protection, logging, alerting, or incident response means M04.

topics.name: Other substantive mitigation
topics.definition: Clear substantive control mechanism outside M01-M08; record a proposed theme.
topics.inclusion_rule: Clear substantive control mechanism outside M01-M08; record a proposed theme.
topics.exclusion_rule: Use a named substantive topic whenever supported.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Clear substantive control mechanism outside M01-M08; record a proposed theme.

topics.name: Unclear or ambiguous mitigation
topics.definition: Genuine mitigation claim but too generic, referential, or evenly multi-mechanism to choose a primary.
topics.inclusion_rule: Genuine mitigation claim but too generic, referential, or evenly multi-mechanism to choose a primary.
topics.exclusion_rule: Use a named substantive topic whenever supported.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Genuine mitigation claim but too generic, referential, or evenly multi-mechanism to choose a primary.

topics.name: Non-substantive mitigation text
topics.definition: No substantive control, including prompt, heading, reference-only passage, bare see-Section-X, bare mitigated or cannot-be-mitigated claim, or extraction artefact.
topics.inclusion_rule: No substantive control, including prompt, heading, reference-only passage, bare see-Section-X, bare mitigated or cannot-be-mitigated claim, or extraction artefact.
topics.exclusion_rule: Use a named substantive topic whenever supported.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: No substantive control, including prompt, heading, reference-only passage, bare see-Section-X, bare mitigated or cannot-be-mitigated claim, or extraction artefact.
